llm.summary: This Tailscale skill is mostly coherent, but some high-impact actions are left untagged even though the safety instructions say untagged actions may run directly.

dimensions.detail: The declared runtime tool scope is limited to Bash(oo *), which is proportionate for an OOMOL connector skill, though the first-time installer examples exceed that declared command scope.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup is disclosed and only recommended after command failure, but it includes remote installer commands such as curl-to-bash or PowerShell irm-to-iex.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: It requires confirmation for actions tagged [write] or [destructive], but several untagged actions appear state-changing or disruptive, including suspend_user, restore_user, rotate_webhook_secret, resend_contact_verification_email, test_webhook, and get_aws_external_id.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill uses an OOMOL-connected Tailscale account with server-side credential injection; this avoids raw token handling but creates a persistent third-party account connection with tailnet authority.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill is purpose-aligned for administering Tailscale through OOMOL, but it exposes broad read, write, secret-creating, role-changing, and destructive tailnet operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing if the connected Tailscale account has admin privileges. Use it only where you are comfortable delegating tailnet administration through OOMOL, and require explicit confirmation for any action that changes users, devices, DNS, keys, webhooks, policy, secrets, or sends external events, even when the skill does not tag that action as write or destructive.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] expected: Using a Tailscale-specific connector for Tailscale requests is coherent with the purpose, but the broad trigger increases impact because the artifact also exposes administrative and destructive operations; the stronger concern is that not all state-changing actions are tagged for confirmation.
